facts.statement: Juratyrant is a genus of tyrannosauroid dinosaur that lived in England during the late Jurassic period.
facts.quote: Juratyrant (meaning "Jurassic tyrant") is a genus of tyrannosauroid dinosaur from the late Jurassic period (early Tithonian age) of England.

facts.statement: The genus Juratyrant contains only one known species, Juratyrant langhami.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Juratyrant langhami, which was once classified as a species of Stokesosaurus.

facts.statement: Juratyrant is known from a single partial skeleton that includes a complete pelvis, parts of the legs, and vertebrae from the neck, back, and tail.
facts.quote: The species is known from a single specimen consisting of an "associated partial skeleton represented by a complete pelvis" as well as a partially complete leg and neck, back and tail vertebrae.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Juratyrant was discovered in Dorset, England, in 1984.
facts.quote: This skeleton was discovered in 1984 in Dorset.

facts.statement: Although mentioned in earlier papers, Juratyrant was not formally described until 2008.
facts.quote: The specimen was mentioned in several papers, but was not formally described until 2008.

facts.statement: The species name langhami honors the fossil collector Peter Langham, who found the specimen.
facts.quote: The species was named in honor of commercial fossil collector Peter Langham, who uncovered the specimen.

facts.statement: Juratyrant lived between 149.3 and 149 million years ago in the Tithonian stage of the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: The specimen was discovered in strata of the Kimmeridge Clay dating from the Tithonian, the final stage of the Late Jurassic, and belonging to the Pectinatites pectinatus ammonite zone, indicating the fossil is between 149.3 and 149 million years old.

facts.statement: The fossil was found in Kimmeridge Clay strata belonging to the Pectinatites pectinatus ammonite zone.
facts.quote: The specimen was discovered in strata of the Kimmeridge Clay dating from the Tithonian, the final stage of the Late Jurassic, and belonging to the Pectinatites pectinatus ammonite zone, indicating the fossil is between 149.3 and 149 million years old.

facts.statement: In 2013, Benson and Brusatte reclassified the species into its own genus and placed it as a sister taxon to Stokesosaurus clevelandi within a clade of basal tyrannosauroids.
facts.quote: It was formally re-classified in its own genus, Juratyrant, by Benson and Stephen L. Brusatte in 2013 and placed as a sister taxon to Stokesosaurus clevelandi in a clade (also including Eotyrannus) of basal tyrannosauroids more advanced than Dilong.

facts.statement: A 2013 study by Loewen et al. suggested Juratyrant belonged to Proceratosauridae based on a shared narrow preacetabular notch.
facts.quote: However, in 2013 Loewen et al. published a cladogram placing Juratyrant as a sister taxon to Stokesosaurus inside Proceratosauridae due to sharing with Sinotyrannus a narrow preacetabular notch.

facts.statement: A 2016 analysis by Brusatte and Carr placed Juratyrant as a tyrannosauroid slightly more advanced than Proceratosauridae and Dilong.
facts.quote: However, a 2016 analysis by Brusatte and Carr utilizing both parsimonious and Bayesian phylogeny placed Stokesosaurus and Juratyrant as tyrannosauroids slightly more advanced than the Proceratosauridae and Dilong.

facts.statement: A 2025 study by Delcourt et al. found that equal-weight phylogenetic analyses placed Juratyrant as an ancestral megaraptoran, which would make it the oldest known record of that group.
facts.quote: In their 2025 revision of the enigmatic Brazilian coelurosaurians Mirischia and Santanaraptor, Delcourt et al. found the placement of Juratyrant to be highly labile to analytical method: Using equal-weight phylogenetic analyses, it resolved as an ancestral megaraptoran outside Megaraptoridae; if this is correct, it would be the oldest record of the Megaraptora at that time.

facts.statement: Zanno and Makovicky estimated in 2013 that Juratyrant weighed up to 648 kg.
facts.quote: In 2013, Zanno and Makovicky estimated that Juratyrant weighed up to 648 kg.

facts.statement: Paul estimated in 2016 that Juratyrant was 5 meters long and weighed 300 kg.
facts.quote: In 2016, Paul listed it at 5 m and 300 kg.

facts.statement: Juratyrant is classified within the superfamily Tyrannosauroidea.
facts.quote: superfamilia: Tyrannosauroidea

facts.statement: Juratyrant is classified within the family Stokesosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Stokesosauridae

facts.statement: Juratyrant langhami lived approximately 150 million years ago in what is now Europe during the late Jurassic Tithonian stage.
facts.quote: Juratyrant langhami es la única especie conocida del género extinto Juratyrant ("tirano del Jurásico") de dinosaurio terópodo tiranosauroide que vivió a finales del período Jurásico durante el Titoniense, hace aproximadamente 150 million years ago, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: The fossil dates to between 149.3 and 149 million years ago based on the Pectinatites pectinatus ammonite zone of the Kimmeridge Clay.
facts.quote: Este ejemplar fue descubierto en los estratos de la arcilla de Kimmeridge que data del Titoniense, la etapa final del Jurásico Superior, y pertenece a la zona del ammonites Pectinatites pectinatus, indicando que el fósil tiene entre 149,3 y 149 millones de años.

facts.statement: Roger Benson originally assigned the species to the genus Stokesosaurus in 2008.
facts.quote: La especie fue originalmente asignada al género Stokesosaurus, como Stokesosaurus langhami, por Roger Benson en 2008.

facts.statement: Benson and Stephen Brusatte reclassified the species into the genus Juratyrant in 2013.
facts.quote: Debido a esto fue reclasificado en su propio género, Juratyrant, en 2013 por Benson y Stephen Brusatte.

facts.statement: The genus Juratyrant was named by Brusatte and Benson in 2013.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Juratyrant (genus), Brusatte and Benson 2013

facts.statement: Juratyrant belongs to the parent group Tyrannosauroidea.
facts.quote: Parent group: Tyrannosauroidea

facts.statement: Juratyrant is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Juratyrant lived during the Tithonian stage, between 145.06 and 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Tithonian to Tithonian (145.06 to 143.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: There is only one recorded fossil occurrence of Juratyrant.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1
